# `reset_setting`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Reset a list of settings to their defaults in one call (firmware 9.75).

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / READ |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.75, handler @0x108ea0 (64-bit build), @0x90420 (32-bit build) |

New in firmware 9.75, app 3.4.0. Resets the named settings (exact names or group prefixes such as stack) to defaults by applying each through the set_setting path, and rolls back on any failure. Keys addressed to the second camera carry the prefix second_camera. and are relayed to it. Keys that cannot be reset are returned in unsupported_keys and are not an error. The resettable key list differs between builds (18 descriptors in the 64-bit build, not 20; 10 keys in the 32-bit build). The 64-bit build refuses exp_ms. items at preparation while Stack is active (259) or a view plan runs (536); the 32-bit planner has no such gate, but exp_ms.stack_l still meets the set_setting Stack busy check. Applying preview.rtsp_quality can meet 524 (AVI recording) and stack.startrail_mode can meet 259 (64-bit). Descriptor defaults are listed in the spec (function-states R4; READ, firmware 9.75). A Setting event follows success. iOS app 3.4.1 adds stack.airplane_line_removal, not a firmware 9.75 descriptor, to its stargazing reset list (READ for the app; the device reply is INFERRED to list it as unsupported).

Side effects: Rewrites the persisted settings for the listed keys, then emits a Setting event. Any failure rolls the whole call back.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"reset_setting"`. [READ] |
| `params` | object | yes | - | Only items is allowed; any other member gives 109. [READ] |
| `params.items` | array<string> | yes | - | Setting names to reset: exact names or group prefixes (stack selects every stack.* key). Characters limited to letters, digits, underscore and dot; empty keys, a leading dot, two dots and duplicates are rejected. A second_camera. prefix routes the key to the second camera. Range: at least 1 item(s). [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (error) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (error) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 107 | params is not an object | `expected object` |
| 109 | params has a member other than items | `unknown member` |
| 102 | items missing, empty, not an array, malformed or duplicated | `bad items` |
| 105 | an element of items is not a string | `expected string` |
| 201 | relay to the second camera failed | `relay failed` |
| 207 | applying a key failed | `apply failed` |
| 210 | second-camera process cannot take the request | `wrong process` |
| 259 | Stack is active and an exp_ms.* key is listed (64-bit build, at preparation) | `stack active` |
| 536 | a view plan is running and an exp_ms.* key is listed (64-bit build, at preparation) | `plan running` |
| 300 | rollback after a failure itself failed | `rollback failed` |
| 524 | a reset transaction is already pending | `busy` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

Busy failures during application, and their outer reply and rollback outcomes, are not fully enumerated; the 107 versus 102 split is unresolved.

## Example

Request, request - READ shape, not captured; values invented:

```json
{"id":81,"method":"reset_setting","params":{"items":["stack","auto_af"]}}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"reset_setting","result":0,"code":0,"id":81,"unsupported_keys":[]}
```
